title: How people detect deepfakes, and where do they go wrong?
introduction: Next you will watch more clips of politicians, some authentic and some AI-generated. Here is what research shows about which cues help and which mislead.

clues.title: Confidence is not a reliable signal
clues.text: Across dozens of studies, people detect deepfakes only slightly better than chance. In a recent study, participants judged 79% of real videos correctly but only 72% of fakes, and felt similarly confident in both cases. The most typical error is accepting a fake without any doubt.

clues.title: Focus on the mouth
clues.text: Many political deepfakes take genuine footage and edit the mouth to sync with the new text. Check whether the lips stay synced with every word, and whether the teeth look blurred. When participants based their judgement on the face, they caught the majority of fake videos.

clues.title: Voice can be supporting evidence
clues.text: Cloned voices can sound real, and they fooled people more often than voice actors did. Pay attention to how things are said. A cloned voice can sound flat, pause in odd places, or carry emotion that doesn't fit the words.

clues.title: Disregard image quality
clues.text: Real videos lose quality each time they are shared on social media, whilst fakes can be perfectly sharp. Judging by quality was right only about half the time, and people who relied on it tended to be overconfident.

clues.title: Verify the source
clues.text: Before accepting or sharing a surprising clip, check who published it first and whether reliable media outlets or independent fact-checkers report it.

questions.question: Which of these best describes the mistakes people made in the study?

options.text: They were often unsure, so they guessed and got it wrong
They were too suspicious and kept calling real videos fake
They believed fakes were real and felt just as sure as usual

questions.feedback: People felt just as confident when they were wrong, so feeling sure doesn't tell you much.

questions.question: Which of these tells you the least about whether a clip is real?

options.text: The voice sounds exactly like the politician
The lips match every single word being said
The emotion in the voice fits the words

questions.feedback: AI can copy a voice almost perfectly, so a voice that sounds right doesn't prove much on its own.

questions.question: A clip is heavily compressed and the face looks a bit pixelated. What should you conclude?

options.text: Probably fake, since AI often leaves pixelated marks like this
Probably real, since deepfakes are usually sharp and clean
Neither, since real and fake clips both get compressed

questions.feedback: Judging by quality was right only about half the time, no better than guessing.
